caption:
Toto wore his brand-new hiking boots straight onto a long trail, and the front of his ankle rubbed and ached more with every step.

New boots are often stiff, and your feet and ankles need time to adjust. A long hike on day one can leave the ankle rubbed or pressed.

Hybi's tip: wear new boots around home first, build up distance bit by bit, avoid lacing too tight, and pair them with cushioned hiking socks.

Numbness or tingling on top of the foot, a swollen or bruised ankle, or no change after two weeks are worth an assessment. Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios can help. Book online via the link in bio
